target.title: fix(auto-reply): self-heal reply-session-init conflict instead of permanently wedging the session
target.body:
## Summary
Fixes #101909.

The reply-session initializer's conflict branch in `src/auto-reply/reply/session.ts` allowed a single stale-snapshot retry and then threw `reply session initialization conflicted for <sessionKey>`. Because initialization never completed, the session-store entry was never committed and the session wedged **permanently** for that `sessionKey`: every subsequent turn re-hit the same conflict, completed tool executions (`exec`/`read`/etc.) had no channel back to the model, and tool-results silently returned empty. It survived gateway restarts (the conflict is keyed to the persistent sessionKey) and cleared only on a fresh session.

This is **runtime-agnostic** and was observed on both the native (Anthropic) runtime and the Codex app-server harness. On the Codex harness the never-written transcript mirror (`<session>.jsonl.codex-app-server.json`, which carries the threadId) is the runtime-specific casualty, but the root cause is the conflict branch failing to recover.

## Fix
The rollover/timeout paths already self-heal by disposing the session's MCP runtime and running the registered harness `reset` hooks (a runtime-agnostic fan-out where each runtime releases its lane and clears its stale native thread binding; the Codex harness additionally lets its mirror rebuild). This change makes the conflict branch reuse that same recovery **once** and retry initialization before giving up:

1. stale-snapshot retry (unchanged — benign concurrent-revision case)
2. if still conflicted: run harness self-heal (`retireSessionMcpRuntime` + `resetRegisteredAgentHarnessSessions`) and retry init once
3. if it still cannot commit: throw with clear context (`…after harness self-heal retry`) instead of leaving the session able to silently return empty tool-results

The decision logic is isolated in a small pure helper (`src/auto-reply/reply/reply-session-init-conflict.ts`) with unit tests.

## Testing
- `npx vitest run src/auto-reply/reply/reply-session-init-conflict.test.ts` → 4/4 pass
- `npx tsc --noEmit -p tsconfig.json` → no type errors in changed files (only pre-existing, unrelated errors in `src/plugins/providers.test.ts`)

## Scope
This addresses the conflict-wedge failure mode. It does not attempt to address a separate operational failure where the Codex app-server child is not running at all — a different cause that presents the same empty-tool-result surface.
